name: Sharmila Ray

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Sharmila Ray is a Kolkata poet and nonfiction essayist writing in English. Her literary work has also crossed into performance: Lyrikline records collaborations between poetry and music, including the sarod. She co-edited “Bridging Continents” with Gopal Lahiri, bringing Indian and American poets into a shared anthology. Her collections include “Scrawls and Scribbles” and the sustained long poem “With Salt and Brine”.

Her Kabita Live poems attend to what larger histories can overlook. “Why do I write” gathers a mother’s sigh, a grandmother’s kitchen and the cracks of an ancestral house into a personal account of poetry as shelter. “Silence” finds meaning in scent, fabric and pauses, while “Different Cities” moves from invisible boundaries and exclusion towards an inward city glimpsed behind closed eyes. Place is both a public world and something carried in memory.
